answer: Hide a fable in the payload. The node embeds a per-account micro-variant - an unused synonym, a whitespace idiom - inside each challenge receipt. If a grove of clones amplifies identical content, the shared variant pins the whole cluster to one seed. To escape, an attacker must generate genuinely unique text per account, costing about as much as hiring real authors, and the receipts sit tundra-cold in signed storage: retrofitting a variant after the fact invalidates the signature.
